headline: ASX dipped 0.7% today as Middle East tensions flare and a landmark AI lawsuit shakes the tech world — but your portfolio holds firm overall, up $30 on the year.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market Shares ETF
movers.note: Solid session today, rising 0.5% to close at $548.53. Broad US market strength from last night carried through — the ETF tracks the entire US sharemarket, so it captured the resilience across mid and small caps even as the NASDAQ pulled back.

movers.name: Global X Artificial Intelligence ETF
movers.note: Up 0.63% today to $16.05, a small positive move despite broader AI sector uncertainty. The fund got a mild lift from positive AI spending sentiment — Nvidia's CapEx cycle commentary and continued AI infrastructure investment kept the mood cautiously upbeat. Still sitting at a -15% loss overall, so this is a welcome green day.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: Edged up 0.35% today to $2.86, a tiny bit of relief for a holding that's down 57% overall. Lithium prices fell 23% recently on oversupply concerns — that's the core weight dragging PLS down. Today's small gain doesn't change the bigger picture; the lithium market remains under real pressure.

movers.name: Vanguard FTSE Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: Rose 0.32% today to $91.95. Emerging markets got a modest lift, possibly helped by Indonesia's upbeat 2027 economic outlook and broader stability in Asian markets. Still slightly underwater overall at -2.78%.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Nudged up 0.38% last night in the US to $227.82. The big news is GTA VI pre-orders have already topped $1 billion — a week before launch — according to Sensor Tower estimates. That's a staggering number and reinforces why TTWO is in a strong position right now.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Essentially flat last night, up a modest 0.17% to $523.88. Microsoft announced a cloud partnership with AI chip startup Cerebras Systems, reinforcing its AI infrastructure push. The stock remains comfortably up 18% from your average buy-in price.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: Fell about 1% last night to $292.52. No major breaking bad news — the broader NASDAQ was soft too, down 0.9%. Underlying fundamentals remain strong: Google Cloud revenue reportedly grew 103% last quarter and the Gemini app hit 1 billion monthly users. The dip looks like general market weakness, not a Google-specific issue.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: Dipped a minor 0.25% today to $77.33, in line with the broader ASX pulling back 0.7%. Nothing specific to VDHG here — it tracks a diversified mix of global shares, so it followed the market down. Still essentially flat on your cost base.

movers.name: BetaShares Diversified All Growth ETF
movers.note: Virtually unchanged today, down just 2 cents to $42.54. This one's as steady as it gets — diversified across global markets, tiny daily moves are the norm. Up 2.24% overall.

watch_today.title: GTA VI pre-orders hit $1 billion — TTWO looking strong
watch_today.detail: GTA VI pre-orders have reportedly topped $1 billion a week before launch, according to Sensor Tower estimates. Even the game's original creators say they haven't been able to play it yet, which is generating massive buzz. This is the moment Take-Two has been building towards for years — if the launch goes well, it's a significant catalyst. For a long-term holder, this is exactly the kind of milestone you've been waiting for. Hold tight.

watch_today.title: PLS still deep underwater — lithium market under pressure
watch_today.detail: Pilbara Minerals edged up 0.35% today, but the broader lithium story remains grim — prices have fallen 23% recently on global oversupply. At -57.6% on your investment, this is the portfolio's biggest drag. The long-term EV demand thesis is still intact, but the recovery timeline keeps stretching. No reason to sell at this price — you'd be locking in a big loss. Hold and wait for the cycle to turn.

watch_today.title: GOOG dipped ~1% last night — but the fundamentals look great
watch_today.detail: Alphabet fell about 1% last night alongside a soft NASDAQ. But step back: Google Cloud reportedly grew 103% last quarter, and the Gemini AI app now has 1 billion monthly users. The long-term story here — cloud, AI, search dominance — is as strong as ever. You're only down ~$5 on a small position. Nothing to worry about; sit tight.

watch_today.title: RBA rate pressure building — watch for household stress signals
watch_today.detail: Multiple news outlets are reporting the RBA cash rate is now at 4.85%, with some economists warning of recession risk for Australian households. A major bank has reportedly called the rate cycle 'done,' suggesting the next move could be a cut. This matters for the broader economy — higher rates squeeze spending, which flows through to company earnings. Worth watching over the next few weeks as more data comes in.

watch_today.title: Major AI lawsuit could freeze development at Google, Microsoft, OpenAI
watch_today.detail: A coalition of nonprofits has filed a landmark lawsuit seeking to halt the development of advanced AI systems at Anthropic, Google, Meta, OpenAI, and SpaceX, citing risks of bioweapon proliferation and cyberattacks. While courts would take months to rule, even the threat of regulatory action creates uncertainty for AI-heavy holdings like GOOG, MSFT, and GXAI.AX. Worth watching as the case develops.

watch_today.title: GXAI.AX had a green day — AI spending sentiment stable
watch_today.detail: Your AI ETF rose 0.63% today to $16.05, a small positive sign. Nvidia's AI infrastructure spending cycle and continued big-tech AI investment are keeping the fund supported, though it's still down 15% overall. The AI lawsuit news (above) is a risk to watch, but for now the sector tailwind is intact. Hold your position.

world.summary: Middle East tensions dominate global headlines with oil tankers on fire in the Strait of Hormuz, while a massive US flight ground stop stranded thousands and Trump reshuffles his Iran diplomacy team. Elsewhere, Goldman Sachs forecasts reasonable global growth for 2027.

stories.title: Oil tankers catch fire in Strait of Hormuz after hitting sea mines
stories.why_it_matters: Iran's Revolutionary Guard (IRGC) says two oil tankers caught fire after hitting sea mines in the Strait of Hormuz — one of the world's most critical shipping chokepoints, through which about 20% of global oil supply passes. Mine warfare in this stretch of water is a serious escalation. Oil prices were already elevated; a sustained blockage or more attacks could push fuel prices higher globally, including at Australian petrol stations. Trump is reportedly discussing Iran directly with Xi and Putin, adding a major geopolitical dimension.

stories.title: Trump pulls VP Vance off Iran talks, redirects focus to 'fraud campaign'
stories.why_it_matters: President Trump has removed Vice President JD Vance from leading Iran nuclear negotiations and redirected him to focus on what Trump is calling a 'fraud campaign.' The move leaves the Middle East in limbo about who is actually running US Iran policy — and markets hate uncertainty in that region. With two tankers already on fire in Hormuz, the lack of clear US diplomatic leadership on Iran is a genuine risk factor for oil prices and regional stability.

stories.title: Ground stop lifted after thousands of US flights stranded
stories.why_it_matters: A ground stop — meaning the aviation authority ordered all departures halted — was imposed across the United States, stranding thousands of flights for several hours before being lifted. The cause hasn't been fully detailed in reports yet, but events like this can ripple through global aviation schedules for days. If you're travelling soon or have family flying through the US, delays are likely still flowing through the system.

stories.title: Goldman Sachs forecasts 2.8% global growth in 2027 as oil prices decline
stories.why_it_matters: Goldman Sachs is forecasting the global economy to grow 2.8% in 2027, with declining oil prices helping ease inflation pressure around the world. That's a reasonably healthy outlook — not booming, but stable. For a long-term investor, steady global growth is a tailwind for diversified ETFs like VDHG and DHHF. Lower oil prices also mean less inflation pressure, which could give central banks room to cut interest rates sooner.

stories.title: Gulf nations open new joint military headquarters in Kuwait amid regional tensions
stories.why_it_matters: Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries — including Saudi Arabia, UAE, and Kuwait — have established a new joint military headquarters in Kuwait as Middle East tensions escalate. This is a significant security development: Gulf states are clearly preparing for the possibility of wider conflict, particularly given the tanker attacks in Hormuz. For Australia, the Gulf region is a key trading partner and major source of our LNG competition — instability there affects global energy markets and our own exports.

markets.summary: The ASX closed down 0.71% today at 9,082 — a broad pullback after a few solid sessions. Last night on Wall Street, the NASDAQ dropped nearly 1% and the S&P 500 fell 0.4%, with tech stocks leading the retreat. Oil is steady near $88.56 a barrel, gold is flat at $3,886, and the Aussie dollar slipped to 67.74 US cents.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: Closed lower today as global uncertainty and Middle East tensions weighed on sentiment.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Pulled back last night — modest decline across the board.

indicators.name: NASDAQ Composite
indicators.note: Tech stocks led the retreat last night, down nearly 1%.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Barely moved despite tanker fires in Hormuz — markets may be pricing in a quick resolution.

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Essentially flat — still at historically elevated levels as a safe haven.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: The Aussie dollar slipped about half a cent — traders may be pricing in rate cut expectations and global risk-off sentiment.

politics.summary: The RBA's interest rate is now at 4.85% and dominating domestic headlines, with one major bank declaring the hiking cycle 'done'. The Albanese government faces mounting pressures on housing, tax reform, and backpacker visa policy. The Greens are adding conditions to Labor's trust tax legislation.

stories.title: Major bank declares RBA rate cycle 'done' as rates hit 4.85%
stories.why_it_matters: At least one major Australian bank is now calling the RBA's interest rate hiking cycle over, with the cash rate sitting at 4.85%. That's one of the highest rates in over a decade, and it's squeezing mortgage holders hard. If this bank is right and the next move is a cut, that would bring relief to millions of Australian borrowers — but it also depends on inflation actually coming down. Watch the RBA's next meeting closely.

stories.title: Australian households face 'horror story' as rates threaten recession
stories.why_it_matters: With the RBA cash rate at 4.85%, commentators are warning that Australian households are under severe financial stress. Higher rates mean bigger mortgage repayments — for someone with a $600,000 mortgage, repayments could be $1,000+ a month more than three years ago. If spending collapses, it could tip the economy into recession. The RBA is walking a tightrope between fighting inflation and not crushing the economy.

stories.title: Government goes back to drawing board on backpacker tax crackdown
stories.why_it_matters: The federal government's plan to crack down on working holiday visas (backpackers) has stalled and gone back to square one. Backpackers fill a critical role in Australian agriculture and hospitality — without them, farms can struggle to harvest crops and regional businesses can't find staff. The policy reversal suggests the government couldn't get it through parliament or faced too much industry blowback. No clear alternative has been announced yet.

stories.title: Greens demand Labor publish names of trust beneficiaries to pass new tax
stories.why_it_matters: The Greens are demanding that Labor publicly release the names of one million Australians who benefit from family trusts — a condition for passing Labor's new trust tax legislation. Trusts are a common tax structure used by wealthy families to distribute income and reduce tax bills. Labor wants to tax them more heavily; the Greens want transparency before they vote for it. This is a classic Greens-Labor negotiation, but it could stall an important revenue measure.

ai.summary: The biggest AI story this week is a landmark lawsuit from nonprofits seeking to freeze development of advanced AI at Google, OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta, and SpaceX over fears of bioweapon and cyberattack risks. Meanwhile, Google dropped Gemini 4 Hydrogen — a new, faster AI model — and the EU is struggling to agree on AI regulation.

stories.title: Landmark lawsuit seeks to halt advanced AI development at Google, OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta and SpaceX
stories.why_it_matters: A coalition of nonprofits has filed a landmark US lawsuit demanding that courts freeze development of the most powerful AI models — the kind being built by OpenAI, Google, Anthropic, Meta, and SpaceX. The plaintiffs argue these 'frontier AI' systems could enable the creation of bioweapons and large-scale cyberattacks. If a court grants even a temporary freeze, it would be the most dramatic regulatory intervention in AI history. For investors in GOOG and MSFT, this is a risk worth watching — though courts typically move slowly and the chance of an immediate freeze is low.

stories.title: Google unveils Gemini 4 Hydrogen — faster and cheaper than rivals
stories.why_it_matters: Google has launched Gemini 4 Hydrogen, described as a new AI model built for speed — competing directly with Anthropic's Claude Sonnet 5.5 and OpenAI's GPT-6.1 Terra. Pricing comparisons put Gemini at roughly $1.50 per million tokens of input versus Claude at $8 — that's a massive cost difference that could attract developers away from rivals. For everyday users, faster and cheaper AI means better tools in Google apps like Gmail, Docs, and Search. Good news for GOOG shareholders.

stories.title: Microsoft announces Cerebras cloud deal — doubling down on AI chips
stories.why_it_matters: Microsoft has struck a cloud deal with Cerebras Systems — a startup that makes AI chips designed to run AI models much faster than conventional chips. Cerebras stock jumped on the news. For Microsoft, this is about reducing dependence on Nvidia and building a faster, cheaper AI infrastructure stack. It's another sign that MSFT is betting heavily on AI as its next major growth engine, and so far that bet is paying off — the stock is up 18% from your buy-in price.

stories.title: New US Congress seen as opportunity to shape national AI policy
stories.why_it_matters: With the new US Congress now seated, think tanks and policy groups are pushing to establish clear federal AI rules before the technology develops further. Currently the US has no comprehensive national AI law — regulation is patchwork and state-by-state. The Cato Institute argues this is a rare window to get sensible rules in place before the next wave of AI capability arrives. How Washington regulates AI will have massive implications for companies like Google, Microsoft, and OpenAI.

sport.summary: The NRL Grand Final is done — the Roosters edged the Knights 19-18 in a thriller at Accor Stadium. NRL 2027 scheduling is already in the news, GTA VI has the gaming world buzzing, and tennis heats up with the Australian Open wildcard race underway.

stories.title: Roosters pip Knights 19-18 in NRL Grand Final classic
stories.why_it_matters: The Sydney Roosters won the 2026 NRL Grand Final, defeating the Newcastle Knights 19-18 in one of the tightest deciders in years at Accor Stadium. A one-point margin — it doesn't get closer than that. The Knights will be devastated having come so close to their first premiership in decades.

stories.title: NRL 2027 Round 1 fixtures revealed — Vegas games and Perth Bears confirmed
stories.why_it_matters: The NRL has revealed its 2027 Round 1 fixtures, confirming that the Las Vegas games are back and the Perth Bears expansion team will make their competition debut. It's a big deal for the game's growth — Vegas games have been a massive hit in drawing international attention to the NRL, and Perth gives the comp a genuine west coast presence for the first time.

stories.title: AFL: Geelong ruck stretchered off, gun midfielder ruled out
stories.why_it_matters: Geelong suffered frightening scenes with their ruck stretchered off the field, while a key midfielder was also ruled out. No specific player names were confirmed in available reports, but injuries to key Cats players would be a major blow heading into the pre-season. Geelong fans will be watching closely for updates.

stories.title: Australian Open wildcard race heats up at NSW Open
stories.why_it_matters: The race for Australian Open wildcards is now on, with a star-studded field heading to the NSW Open. Wildcards are coveted spots that allow players who haven't qualified through rankings to enter the AO draw — a big deal for emerging Aussie talent. The tournament is a final chance for local players to prove they deserve a spot at the year's first Grand Slam.
